message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy‑paste into a terminal or a script to pull **only the `id` and `context` fields** for community comments on the domain `test4.org`.  
The request uses the continuation cursor `cur456` and your API key `key123`.

---

## 1.  REST‑style HTTP request (curl)

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&cursor=cur456&fields=id,context" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

### What each part does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments` | Base endpoint for comments |
| `?domain=test4.org` | Filters comments to the requested domain |
| `&cursor=cur456` | Tells the API to continue from the last page you fetched |
| `&fields=id,context` | Instructs the API to return **only** the `id` and `context` attributes |
| `-H "Authorization: Bearer key123"` | Passes your API key in the Authorization header (replace with the actual header format your service expects) |
| `-H "Accept: application/json"` | Requests JSON output |

> **Tip:** If your API expects the key in a query string instead of a header, change the URL to:
> ```bash
> https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&cursor=cur456&fields=id,context&api_key=key123
> ```

---

## 2.  Python `requests` example

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments"
params = {
    "domain": "test4.org",
    "cursor": "cur456",
    "fields": "id,context"
}
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer key123",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
response.raise_for_status()          # will raise an error if the request failed
data = response.json()

# `data` now contains only the `id` and `context` for each comment
print(data)
```

---

## 3.  What the response looks like

```json
{
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt_001",
      "context": {
        "author": "alice",
        "text": "Great post!"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt_002",
      "context": {
        "author": "bob",
        "text": "I disagree."
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // if there are more pages
}
```

Only the `id` and `context` fields appear; all other comment metadata is omitted.

---

## 4.  Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Wrong header format** | Some APIs use `x-api-key: key123` instead of `Authorization`. Check the docs. |
| **Missing `fields` param** | If you forget `fields=id,context`, the API will return the full comment object. |
| **Cursor typo** | Ensure `cur456` matches exactly what the previous page returned. |
| **Rate limits** | If you hit a 429 error, add a delay or use the `Retry-After` header. |

---

### Done!  
Run the curl command or the Python snippet, and you’ll get a lean payload containing just the IDs and context of the community comments for `test4.org`. Happy coding!
